research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic research-source confidence only: direct official GOV.UK/HSE verification, 2026 regulatory/currentness checks where available, planning-vs-building-regulations separation, programme/pipeline-vs-delivery controls, indicative-vs-exact geography, transitional commencement, capacity and cross-regime fail-closed gates. Not parcel-level accuracy.

verification.method: Direct official-web verification plus repository duplicate searches

official_sources.name: Climate change planning guidance
official_sources.fact: Planning guidance requires mitigation and adaptation to be integrated into plan-making and decisions, including resilience, cooling, green infrastructure and avoiding maladaptation.
official_sources.gate: Climate-policy relevance is not parcel-level climate resilience, planning permission or proof that a specific design complies.

official_sources.name: Renewable and low carbon energy planning guidance
official_sources.fact: Government guidance sets planning considerations for renewable and low-carbon energy including solar, wind, hydropower and battery energy storage systems.
official_sources.gate: Renewable-energy policy support is not evidence of grid capacity, site consent, land control or project viability.

official_sources.name: NPPF chapter 14 climate change flooding and coastal change
official_sources.fact: The current NPPF climate chapter sets national planning policy for climate mitigation/adaptation, flood risk and coastal change.
official_sources.gate: National policy must not be promoted to a parcel-specific flood, climate, energy or permission conclusion.

official_sources.name: National Policy Statement EN-3 2025
official_sources.fact: EN-3 2025 came into force on 6 January 2026 and sets assessment policy for nationally significant renewable-energy infrastructure.
official_sources.gate: NSIP policy does not prove a parcel hosts an NSIP, has development consent, grid connection or construction readiness.

official_sources.name: Heat Networks Delivery Unit
official_sources.fact: HNDU guidance updated 30 March 2026 describes support, zoning work and a future heat-network zoning pipeline.
official_sources.gate: Pipeline or opportunity-area status is not statutory zone designation, connection capacity, funding award or parcel obligation.

official_sources.name: Heat networks regulation technical standards
official_sources.fact: DESNZ guidance updated 16 February 2026 describes upcoming regulatory technical requirements and the Heat Network Technical Assurance Scheme.
official_sources.gate: Technical-standard guidance is not proof a network is authorised, compliant, built or available to a target site.

official_sources.name: Heat networks metering and billing regulations
official_sources.fact: Guidance updated 11 February 2026 records the 2026 market-framework changes and Ofgem's regulatory role for heat networks.
official_sources.gate: Regulatory authorisation duties do not prove a local network exists, has spare capacity or can connect a parcel.

official_sources.name: Heat network zoning collection
official_sources.fact: The collection explains Energy Act powers, January 2026 consultation outcomes and national zoning-model work.
official_sources.gate: Potential zones, pilots and policy material must not be treated as final statutory zone boundaries or a connection mandate.

official_sources.name: Heat network zoning maps
official_sources.fact: DESNZ states the published maps are indicative early outputs showing potential heat-network zones.
official_sources.gate: Indicative opportunity maps must not be promoted to statutory zoning, exact parcel coverage or guaranteed future network delivery.

official_sources.name: Heat network zoning overview
official_sources.fact: The overview explains how heat-network zones are intended to identify areas where networks could be a low-cost decarbonisation solution.
official_sources.gate: An overview or modelled opportunity is strategic context, not legal parcel status or connection capacity.

official_sources.name: Heat network zoning promotional resources
official_sources.fact: Promotional resources were updated 21 January 2026 to explain heat-network zoning proposals.
official_sources.gate: Promotional material is not operative legislation, a designation decision or parcel-specific evidence.

official_sources.name: Green Heat Network Fund guidance
official_sources.fact: GHNF guidance updated 10 June 2026 describes capital-grant support and application requirements for low-carbon heat networks.
official_sources.gate: Funding eligibility or an application round is not evidence a project received funding, consent or parcel-level service.

official_sources.name: Heat Networks Zoning Pilot
official_sources.fact: The pilot documents work across 28 English towns and cities and notes outputs used to identify where heat networks may grow.
official_sources.gate: Pilot participation or model output is not statutory designation, committed investment or exact parcel connectivity.

official_sources.name: Heat networks optimisation guidance
official_sources.fact: Guidance updated 25 February 2026 supports operators in improving existing heat-network performance.
official_sources.gate: Operational optimisation guidance does not prove a network serves a parcel or has spare capacity.

official_sources.name: Approved Document L 2026
official_sources.fact: Approved Document L 2026 supports Part L energy and greenhouse-gas requirements for buildings subject to the 2026 standards.
official_sources.gate: Building-regulation compliance is separate from planning permission and does not establish parcel development capacity.

official_sources.name: Approved Document F 2026
official_sources.fact: Approved Document F 2026 supports ventilation requirements under Part F for buildings subject to the new standards.
official_sources.gate: Ventilation compliance is a building-regulations matter, not evidence of planning permission or site suitability.

official_sources.name: Future Homes and Buildings Standards Circular 01/2026
official_sources.fact: The 24 March 2026 circular sets out implementation of amendments following the Future Homes and Buildings Standards.
official_sources.gate: A regulatory circular does not by itself identify which transitional standard applies to an exact project without its dates and building-work facts.

official_sources.name: Future Homes and Buildings Standards Circular letter
official_sources.fact: The circular letter states most 2026 amendments come into force on 24 March 2027, with specified higher-risk-building provisions later and transitional arrangements applying.
official_sources.gate: Future commencement dates and transition rules must not be treated as already-applicable requirements for every current project.

official_sources.name: Energy performance methodologies notice 2026
official_sources.fact: The 24 March 2026 notice updates approved national calculation methodologies and reflects SAP 10.3.
official_sources.gate: An approved calculation methodology is not an EPC result, as-built performance, planning permission or parcel-level energy score.

official_sources.name: New-building energy calculation methodology 2026
official_sources.fact: The notice sets approved calculation methodologies for new buildings in England under Building Regulations 2010.
official_sources.gate: Methodology availability does not establish that a particular design passes Part L or that a site is developable.

official_sources.name: Future Homes and Buildings Standards impact assessments
official_sources.fact: The March 2026 impact assessments estimate costs, benefits and wider impacts of changes to Parts L, F and 6.
official_sources.gate: National impact-assessment estimates are not parcel-level construction costs, viability or permission evidence.

official_sources.name: RPC opinion on Future Homes and Buildings Standards impact assessments
official_sources.fact: The RPC published its March 2026 opinion on the impact assessments, distinguishing its assessment of evidence from the policy itself.
official_sources.gate: A regulatory evidence-quality rating must not be converted into a conclusion that the underlying standards are invalid or inapplicable.

official_sources.name: Building regulations circulars collection
official_sources.fact: The collection was updated 9 July 2026 and lists current circulars including Future Homes and Buildings Standards material.
official_sources.gate: A circular index is provenance/currentness evidence, not project-specific compliance or approval.

official_sources.name: Building control approval for higher-risk buildings
official_sources.fact: Guidance updated 1 April 2026 explains BSR building-control approval for higher-risk building work and explicitly distinguishes planning permission.
official_sources.gate: Building-control approval and planning permission are separate; neither may be inferred from the other.

official_sources.name: Criteria for new higher-risk buildings
official_sources.fact: Guidance explains statutory criteria for determining whether a new building falls within the higher-risk design-and-construction regime.
official_sources.gate: Height/storey/use screening must use exact building facts and does not itself indicate planning acceptability.

official_sources.name: Higher-risk building occupation criteria
official_sources.fact: Guidance explains the separate in-occupation higher-risk-building definition and regulatory duties.
official_sources.gate: Occupation-regime status is not planning permission, building-control completion or a parcel-development score.

official_sources.name: HSE fire safety and planning
official_sources.fact: HSE states it is a statutory consultee for relevant planning applications and separates planning fire-safety advice from Building Regulations compliance.
official_sources.gate: HSE consultation or pre-application advice is not planning permission or building-regulations approval.

official_sources.name: Fire safety and high-rise residential buildings
official_sources.fact: Planning gateway one requires fire statements for specified relevant applications and statutory consultation in defined cases.
official_sources.gate: A fire statement demonstrates consideration of planning fire-safety matters; it is not approval, Building Regulations compliance or permission.

official_sources.name: Approved Document O overheating FAQ
official_sources.fact: Approved Document O guidance addresses overheating risk in new residential buildings and defines its scope.
official_sources.gate: Overheating compliance is proposal/building-specific and must not be inferred from climate-policy context or parcel location.

official_sources.name: Building-safety remediation regulatory regimes annex
official_sources.fact: The annex summarises the Building Safety Regulator's higher-risk-building regime, registration and risk-management duties.
official_sources.gate: Regulatory regime status is separate from planning permission, remediation completion and site development capacity.
